findings.message: NEW — CHANGELOG 0.4.5 says 'eleven per-feature writers'; the release's own CLOSURE drift and the census test both say thirteen.
findings.detail_md:
`CHANGELOG.md` (added at `81e35dd1`), `### Added`, first bullet:

> **One atomic-write primitive** (`core/atomic_write.py`) replacing **eleven** per-feature writers…

The same delta's `specs/releases/v0.4.5/CLOSURE.md` carries a named drift `### fr2-thirteen-writers-not-eleven`:

> SPEC FR2 and TASKS enumerate **eleven** writers (8 named + 3 inline). The T-045-13 scan found **thirteen** … 13 → 1, confirmed by the census test.

Confirmed at HEAD independently: `tests/unit/core/test_atomic_write_census.py:9-10,130-131` documents *'the eight T-045-13 shims, the three inline `.tmp` writers, plus the two writers T-045-13's sweep discovered'* — 8 + 3 + 2 = **13**; 19 non-test modules now import the primitive. The CHANGELOG therefore publishes the pre-scan hand-written figure the release explicitly recorded as wrong.

**Why it is a finding and not pedantry.** The `pypi-distribution` memory atom makes the CHANGELOG the *complete* lineage record, and PyPI descriptions are immutable per release — an in-place fix later requires a version bump. Correcting it costs one character now and is impossible to correct in place once published. No security impact: the number describes a completed consolidation, not a control.
findings.fix_recommendation: software-engineer (or whoever owns the mint commit): change 'eleven' to 'thirteen' in the CHANGELOG 0.4.5 `### Added` bullet before the deploy PR, matching CLOSURE `### fr2-thirteen-writers-not-eleven` and the census test. findings.message: NEW — the bug-governance memory atom calls the masked set 'every schema free-text field'; the shipped tuple also masks the enum `severity` and the routing `context`.
findings.detail_md:
`specs/memory/product/sdd/sdd-bug-backlog-governance.md` (rewritten at `e514e679`) adds `### The write seam`, whose summary reads *'masks every schema **free-text** field with the same operator denylist the push boundary refuses on'*, and later *'The field set is the schema mirror the serializer itself uses.'*

The second clause is exactly right. The first understates the blast radius. At HEAD, `core/models/bugs.py:204-221` `_OPTIONAL_STR_FIELDS` — the tuple `redact()` iterates at `:350-360` and `to_dict()` iterates for serialization — contains `severity`, `surface`, `component` and `context` alongside the genuinely free-text fields. `severity` is a **schema enum** (`LOW|MEDIUM|HIGH|CRITICAL`) and `context` is **routing metadata**; neither is free text, and both are rewritten to `[REDACTED-TERM]` if an operator term is a case-insensitive substring of the value.

This is the documentation face of the carried MEDIUM and its sibling LOW below: the code masks structured fields, the ledger is append-only, and validation happens on the *unredacted* object — so a colliding term lands a schema-violating row permanently. Recording the mechanism in memory as free-text-only makes it likely that a future reader concludes `severity` is out of reach and closes the MEDIUM as theoretical. Not exploitable in this workspace today (0 of the live 18 terms collide with the enum, re-verified this session); no consumer of `BugEvent.context` exists in the service fold.
findings.fix_recommendation: product-engineer, at the next MEMORY window: replace 'every schema free-text field' with the accurate scope — the serializer's own optional-string mirror, which includes the enumerated `severity` and the routing `context`, `surface`, `component` — and cross-reference the open ordering question. Do not add a second hand-kept list; the schema mirror is the right mechanism and the wording is what needs fixing.

findings.message: Verified NOT a regression — the CHANGELOG's 'manifest-tracked projections' phrasing for the LAW class; the pre-release predicate had no manifest arm either.
findings.detail_md:
`CHANGELOG.md` `### Changed` reads *'LAW path class classified by origin (workspace-root law family + manifest-tracked projections)'*, and `CLOSURE.md` `### fr1-landed-without-the-manifest-arm` records that the landed fix has **no manifest arm at all**. I checked whether that removal *un-protected* anything, rather than accepting the closure's own account.

**It did not.** `git show 68658783:…/gate_policy.py` shows the pre-release `_is_law_path` was already exact-path + harness-dir with **no manifest lookup**; the only behavioural delta is the removal of the `ctx_rel in _LAW_BASENAMES` branch, i.e. the `repos/<slug>/AGENTS.md` LAW -> MUTATING loosening I reviewed and approved at `395bfb35`. Probing the live classifier confirms the shape on both sides of the release:

| path | class |
|---|---|
| `DADAIA.md`, `AGENTS.md` | **LAW** |
| `.codex/DADAIA.md` | **LAW** |
| `.claude/agents/security-reviewer.md` | UNGATED (before and after) |
| `.claude/skills/<s>/SKILL.md` | UNGATED (before and after) |
| `repos/<slug>/AGENTS.md` | MUTATING (was LAW) |
| `specs/releases/*/verdicts/*.handoff.json` | MUTATING |

So LAW = a law **basename** at a fixed **origin**; manifest tracking confers no gate protection and never did — non-law projections are governed by the agent write allowlists and by `public doctor` drift detection, per `DADAIA.md` §8. The CHANGELOG parenthetical is loose prose about which files the family covers, not a false control claim, and the memory atom `sdd-gate-v3.md` states it precisely in this same delta (*'`.dadaia/agentic/manifest.json` classifies UNGATED and is never consulted'*, *'`classify_path` performs zero I/O on that decision'*). A1.7 (CWE-284) holds by construction. Recorded so the check is on the record; no action.
findings.fix_recommendation: No action — the authoritative surface (the memory atom) is already precise.

findings.message: Mint 0.4.5 without publish: the control is the release-gate environment, verified sound, time-bounded and OIDC-only.
findings.detail_md:
The delta bumps `pyproject.toml` `0.4.4 -> 0.4.5` and documents the minted-unpublished shape (operator order O5). I verified the control rather than the intent, because after the `develop -> main` merge the pipeline **will** fire:

- `.github/workflows/release.yml`: `publish` has `needs: [check, build, approve]`; `approve` carries `environment: release-gate` with `timeout-minutes: 60`. Withholding the approval is a supported terminal outcome — and the 60-minute timeout means a run cannot sit indefinitely waiting for an accidental click.
- `publish` uses `environment: pypi` with `permissions: id-token: write` and `pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish` — **OIDC trusted publishing, no long-lived PyPI token** in the repo or its secrets. Every action in the job is pinned by commit sha.
- The `v0.4.5` git tag is created **inside** `publish`, so no approval means no tag; `git tag -l v0.4.5` is empty at HEAD.
- `pyproject.toml` is the sole restatement of the number (`grep -rn` finds no second source), so the mint cannot drift between files.
- `.github/**` is **untouched** across the whole reviewed range — the pipeline that will run is the one already reviewed.

`CLOSURE.md` `## Ship-without-publish record` correctly leaves the three A16.8 verifications open, to be filled at T-045-41 after the merge. That is the right shape: the evidence does not exist yet and is not fabricated.
findings.fix_recommendation: operator: when the `develop -> main` merge fires `release.yml`, leave the `approve` job unapproved on the `release-gate` environment and let it time out; then record the three A16.8 verifications in CLOSURE at T-045-41. Do not create a `v0.4.5` tag by hand — a hand-made tag would make the `check` job skip a future legitimate publish of that number.

findings.message: Marker trace: `81e35dd1` landed under T-045-40 while T-045-40's marker stayed `[ ]` — the reservation trace for the mint commit is missing.
findings.detail_md:
`DADAIA.md` §6 requires flipping `[ ]` -> `[-]` *before* writing, as the auditable trace of who took what. In this delta the discipline is followed twice (`7b80e646` and `bb96253a` flip T-045-37/T-045-38 to `[-]`; their docs commits flip to `[x]`), and skipped once: `81e35dd1` (`chore(T-045-40): mint 0.4.5`) touches only `CHANGELOG.md` and `pyproject.toml`, and `TASKS.md:980` still reads `- [ ] **T-045-40**` at HEAD.

T-045-40 is a compound `[git]` task (version bump **and** the PR to `develop`), so `[x]` would be wrong — `[-]` is the state the executed half calls for. `T-045-35` sits at `[-]` correctly for the same reason. The BACKLOG ledger commit `18638d3b` carries no task id by design: CLOSURE's `## Record-only observations` explicitly rules the `CONSUMED -> DELIVERED` flip a PM closure step off that document.

Governance/traceability only — no security impact; recorded because the marker set is part of the artifact this delta ships.
findings.fix_recommendation: project-manager or the mint's author: flip T-045-40 to `[-]` on the branch to match its landed half, or state in CLOSURE's rc ledger that the mint half landed under a `[ ]` marker by intent. Either closes the trace; the flip is one character.

findings.message: Environment observation — `public doctor` reports the installed codex-cli is one version past the live-certified hook-fire probe.
findings.detail_md:
Surfaced by `dadaia public doctor` during this scan, unrelated to the delta and pre-existing:

> `[info] codex:trust-boundary` — installed codex-cli **0.145.0** has not been live-certified for hook-fire behavior (last certified: **0.144.4**); the interactive-vs-headless claim is UNVERIFIED for this version … the git chokepoints remain independent defense-in-depth regardless.

findings.message: CARRIED — FR6 validates before redacting; the persisted bug row is never the validated one (CWE-20).
findings.detail_md:
Unchanged by this delta — no commit since `395bfb35` touches `specs/bugs/` or `cli/commands/bugs.py`; re-stated so this verdict stands alone.

`dadaia_workspace/cli/commands/bugs.py:245-265` builds `payload = model.to_dict()` from the **unredacted** model, validates that against `bug-event-v1.schema.json`, and only then calls `service.append_event(model)`, where `features/bugs/service.py:93` applies `event.redact(self._denylist_terms)`. The object written to the append-only ledger is never the object that was validated.

Harmless while `redact()` touched free text only. FR6 widened it: `core/models/bugs.py:350-360` scrubs the whole `_OPTIONAL_STR_FIELDS` tuple (`core/models/bugs.py:204-221`), which includes the structured `severity`, `context`, `surface`, `component`. A denylist term that is a case-insensitive substring of a severity value rewrites `severity` to `[REDACTED-TERM]` and lands a row violating the schema's `enum: [LOW, MEDIUM, HIGH, CRITICAL]`, undetected, in a store that by law is never rewritten.

**Not exploitable in this workspace today**, re-verified this session: 0 of the live 18 operator terms collide with the enum. The defect is the ordering, which makes correctness depend on operator-supplied data the code never constrains.
findings.fix_recommendation: Validate the object actually persisted: redact before `to_dict()`/validate in `cli/commands/bugs.py`, or move schema validation inside `BugService.append_event` after `event.redact(...)`. One redaction pass, one validation pass, same object — do not reintroduce the double-redact AM-1 removed.

findings.message: CARRIED — FR6 masks the `context` field: 5 of 7 local context slugs redact to [REDACTED-TERM] in consumer bug ledgers.
findings.detail_md:
Unchanged by this delta; carried as intake. Concrete consequence of the same `_OPTIONAL_STR_FIELDS` widening: checked against the live denylist and the local `repos/` set, **5 of 7** context slugs match a term, so in those contexts every future `dadaia bugs append --context <slug>` persists `"context": "[REDACTED-TERM]"`. `dadaia-workspace` itself is unaffected, so this repo's ledger stays clean.

Masking a private slug out of a committed ledger is arguably the intended privacy outcome; the issue is that it arrived as a side effect of 'mirror the whole optional-str tuple' rather than a stated decision, and it silently drops routing metadata. See also the NEW LOW above: the memory atom now documents the seam but calls the field set free-text, which hides this consequence rather than recording it.
findings.fix_recommendation: Record an explicit ADR: either accept context masking as intended FR6 behaviour and say so in the memory atom, or exclude the enumerated/structured fields (`severity`, `context`, `surface`, `component`) from the denylist pass while keeping them in the IP/home-path pass — derived from the schema's own markers, never a second hand-kept list.

findings.message: CARRIED — FR8 leaves the default `specs init` path outside the CWE-59 symlink refusal.
findings.detail_md:
Unchanged by this delta; carried as intake. `dadaia_workspace/cli/commands/specs.py:329`:

```python
target = _resolve_specs_dir(specs_dir) if specs_dir else Path.cwd() / "specs"
```

Only the **explicit** `--specs-dir` arm reaches `core/specs_resolver.py:157`'s `path.is_symlink()` refusal. The `None` arm keeps the raw `Path.cwd() / "specs"`, and the guard below it refuses only the Workspace-Root case, never a symlink — so `cd repos/<slug> && dadaia specs init` with a planted `specs` symlink still scaffolds through it, the exact class T-044-40 closed for the explicit arm. LOW: local only, needs an attacker-planted symlink plus an operator running `init` there, and the impact is creation of fixed-name template files, not disclosure. Standing note: `is_symlink()` checks the final component only — a symlinked *parent* is still followed (pre-existing).
findings.fix_recommendation: Apply the same refusal to the default arm — check `is_symlink()` on the computed `Path.cwd() / 'specs'` before scaffolding, reusing the resolver's existing refusal message rather than adding a second one (A8.2).

findings.message: CARRIED — core/atomic_write.py: no O_EXCL on the temp sibling, preserve_mode defaults to False (CWE-377 / CWE-732).
findings.detail_md:
Unchanged by this delta; carried as intake. Neither is a regression. `dadaia_workspace/core/atomic_write.py:60-75`.

1. **No `O_EXCL`.** The temp sibling is created with `tmp.write_bytes()` / `tmp.write_text()`, which follow symlinks and do not fail on an existing path. The `uuid4().hex` name makes pre-creation infeasible, and the file is a sibling of the destination rather than in a world-writable temp dir, so the classic CWE-377 race does not apply. `os.replace` does not follow a symlinked destination — a symlinked target is replaced by a regular file, the safe outcome.

2. **`preserve_mode=False` default.** A write over an existing restrictive-mode file widens it to the umask default. Verified non-regressive: all replaced writers had exactly this behaviour; law files are re-chmod'd `0o444` at `infrastructure/install_helpers.py:170-173`; executable projections chmod `0o755` after write and `infrastructure/public_assets.py:1322-1335` reports a cleared exec bit as repairable drift.
findings.fix_recommendation: Optional hardening, not required: create the temp sibling with `os.open(..., O_CREAT|O_EXCL|O_WRONLY)`, and document that a caller writing a mode-sensitive destination must pass `preserve_mode=True` (the callers that need it already do).

findings.message: CARRIED — the narrowed slug layer misses a private slug glued inside a hyphenated/dotted identifier; the operator denylist remains the authoritative net.
findings.detail_md:
Unchanged by this delta; the ruled trade from `395bfb35`. `compile_slug_patterns` matches a slug as a **whole token** only: bare prose, `repos/<slug>/`, whitespace/quote/paren bounds and sentence-end period all still **BLOCK**, while `x-<slug>-y`, `<slug>.internal` and `<slug>.git` now pass. The operator-denylist layer — a pure case-insensitive **substring** match with no boundary restriction — is untouched and catches every genuinely private name in all of those shapes.

**Improved by this delta, and worth saying:** the residual is now **stated product truth** rather than a silent side effect. `specs/memory/product/sdd/sdd-gate-v3.md` (rewritten at `e514e679`) names it explicitly — *'`<slug>-x`, `x-<slug>`, `<slug>.ext` and `pkg.<slug>` are other identifiers'* — and CLOSURE `## Intake candidates` item 10 carries the clone-URL sub-class (`…/<slug>.git`) to the operator. Documenting an accepted trade at the surface a future reader will consult is the correct disposition.
findings.fix_recommendation: Two things, neither blocking: (a) operational — a repo slug that is itself sensitive must be registered in `.dadaia/states/privacy_denylist.json`, never relied upon via the auto-derived layer, which does not exist on CI at all; (b) 0.5.0 — consider letting a dotted continuation still fire for a known VCS/network suffix (`.git`, `.internal`, `.local`), which recovers the realistic residual without reintroducing the basename/bug-id false positive. Do not add an allowlist (A4.1).

findings.message: CARRIED — FR1/FR2/FR6/FR7/FR8 and the certify capping stand unchanged; CVE and IaC lanes have no input across the whole release range.
findings.detail_md:
Restated so this verdict stands alone; every item was verified at `395bfb35` and no executed path changed since.

**FR7 (CWE-117).** `core/models/bugs.py:255`'s `_UNSAFE_FORMAT_CHARS_RE` cross-checks against CPython's `str.splitlines()` terminator set: every terminator except `\n`/`\r` is stripped (`\v`/`\f`, `\x1c-\x1e` inside `\x0e-\x1f`, `\x85` inside the C1 range, plus `\u2028`/`\u2029`). TAB/LF/CR survive, and `json.dumps(..., ensure_ascii=False)` escapes the whole C0 range, so no field value can fragment a JSONL line the reader splits on a literal newline. The C1 range is not escaped by `ensure_ascii=False`, which is why stripping it is load-bearing. A7.6 ordering (strip -> IP -> home -> denylist) closes split-term evasion.

**FR1 (CWE-284).** `features/spec_context/gate_policy.py:256-268` is pure string splitting over two module-level frozensets bound at import from `core/workspace_layout.py:84-89`; `classify_path` evaluates LAW first with zero I/O and no manifest read — re-probed live this session (table in the INFO above).

**FR2 / FR8 / certify:** the carried LOWs above, plus the CWE-532 capping in `features/certification/service.py:84-125` (parsed, cwd-masked, 200-char-capped detail; residual: only cwd is seeded into the `Redactor`, acceptable for an upstream auth-rejection message).

**CVE / IaC lanes.** `git diff --name-only 68658783..18638d3b` over `poetry.lock`, `requirements*.txt`, `uv.lock`, `.github/**`, `Dockerfile*`, `docker-compose*`, `*.tf` is **empty**; `pyproject.toml` differs on the version line alone. 0 new dependencies, 0 CVE findings by absence of a changed manifest — stated as absence of input, not as an unrun scan.

findings.detail_md:
`dadaia bugs stats` at HEAD: **495 total, 476 resolved, 13 superseded, 1 open, 1 deferred, 4 rejected**. The ledger is **byte-identical to the reviewed range** — `git log 395bfb35..HEAD -- specs/bugs/` is empty and the worktree is clean — so this delta neither opened nor closed a bug.

**This delta.** +0 production lines, +0 branches, +0 flags, +0 code paths. It cannot increase the bug surface of any feature. What it does do is move two structural narrowings out of review prose and into the memory atoms every future agent reads: LAW decided by **origin** with zero I/O (so no writable inventory can promote or demote a security decision), and the **whole-token** slug matcher **with its residual shapes named in the same paragraph**. Under the standing order, recording an accepted trade at the surface a future reader consults is the anti-puxadinho move — the alternative is a silent trade that the next reviewer rediscovers as a finding.

**The release it closes** (unchanged assessment): FR2 collapses 13 hand-kept atomic-write idioms into one `core` leaf; FR6 replaces a twice-missed hand-kept field list with the schema-mirror tuple; FR1 removes a branch from the LAW predicate; FR7 narrows an over-broad strip; the T-045-35 fix is +2/-1 with no allowlist. Each is a deletion or a collapse. CLOSURE `## Standing-order verdict record` independently reports five recurrence chains made structurally unrepresentable, and its one honest 'surface increased' entry (FR7's landing, closed by the F1 rework) matches what I found at `395bfb35`. The three new LOWs in this verdict are documentation-accuracy, none of which adds executable surface.
